title: Function Review: Power Tools
story: You've built dozens of functions across these lessons. Now it's time to prove your mastery by building a showcase — six functions spanning math, strings, booleans, and randomness — and demonstrating every single one in a clean, organized program.
why: This review consolidates all function patterns learned so far: calculations, string manipulation, Boolean checks, random generation, and void procedures — all called from a single orchestrated main().
analogy: This review is like a tool belt inspection before a big project. You lay out each tool on the workbench: absolute value (tape measure), minimum (level), shout (megaphone), in_range (stud finder), roll_dice (random number generator), print_header (label maker). Each tool works independently, but together they form a complete kit ready for any job.
try_it: Add a seventh function of your own design — something from an earlier lesson or a completely original idea. Options: `is_palindrome`, `factorial`, `fizzbuzz`, `count_vowels`, or invent something new like `grade_to_letter(score: Int) -> Str`.
tips: Use the stdlib when available: math.abs_int, math.min_int, string.str_upper are built and tested
in_range uses `and` to combine two comparisons into one Boolean check
roll_dice returns 1-6 inclusive because math.random_range is inclusive on both ends
Void functions like print_header do work but return nothing — perfect for formatting output
common_mistakes: Reimplementing stdlib functions instead of calling them — use math.abs_int, not your own abs
Confusing math.min_int with math.max_int — min returns the smaller of two numbers
Forgetting to handle the Boolean return of in_range — capture it with let or use it in an if
Adding a return type to print_header — void functions have no -> ReturnType
